Barley malting-premium value schedule

Source: R/grain-value-library.R
barley_malting_premium.Rd

The barley counterpart to wheat_protein_bands(): a price per tonne that carries a malting premium when grain protein falls inside the malting window and drops to the feed price outside it. Malting barley is the textbook two-sided quality payoff – protein that is too low or too high both miss the malting grade – which a single rising step schedule cannot express, so this schedule pays the premium only across the central band.

Usage

barley_malting_premium(
  window = c(9.5, 12.5),
  feed_price = 280,
  malting_premium = 60
)

Arguments

window

A length-two numeric vector c(low, high) giving the malting protein window in percent (default c(9.5, 12.5)).

feed_price

The feed price in dollars per tonne paid outside the window (default an illustrative 280).

malting_premium

The premium in dollars per tonne added to the feed price inside the window (default an illustrative 60).

Value

A decideR::grade_band_value schedule: a vectorised function from a protein outcome to its dollar-per-tonne payoff, paying feed_price + malting_premium inside the window and feed_price outside.

Details

The default window is the broad malting protein window in percent and the default prices are an illustrative feed price and malting premium in dollars per tonne. The window shape (a premium inside an acceptance band, feed outside) follows the published Barley Australia / Grain Trade Australia malting receival conventions; the dollar values are illustrative and not receival prices. Supply current prices for a real decision.

References

Barley Australia and Grain Trade Australia malting barley receival standards (the malting protein window). Dollar values are illustrative.

See also

wheat_protein_bands() for the wheat counterpart; plan_grade_target() for the decision that consumes it.

Other grain-value: n_rate_economics(), wheat_protein_bands()

Examples

v <- barley_malting_premium()
v(c(8.0, 10.5, 13.0))
#> [1] 280 340 280
v
#> <grade_band_value> 3 bands
#>                 band value
#>          feed (<9.5)   280
#>  malting [9.5, 12.5)   340
#>        feed (>=12.5)   280
